claims.text: Controlled Ti addition and thermal processing will induce nanoscale BCC-rich segregation within an FCC Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix.
The secondary BCC-rich phase will be enriched in Ti and Fe.
The Ti-induced BCC-rich phase can remain coherent with the FCC matrix.
Interfacial exchange coupling between the FCC matrix and BCC-rich phase will increase magnetic anisotropy and coercivity.
The dual-phase alloy will exhibit a coercive field exceeding 100 Oe.
The dual-phase alloy will retain a Curie temperature above 300 K.
Single-phase FCC Fe-Co-Ni-Ti has low coercivity because its orbital moments and magnetic anisotropy are suppressed.
An appropriate single-phase FCC Fe-Co-Ni-Ti baseline has coercivity below 20 Oe and Curie temperature above 300 K.
Low-spin fluctuations stabilize FCC CoCrFeMnNi while producing low magnetic anisotropy.
Ti-induced lattice distortion and chemical ordering will stabilize the secondary BCC phase between 300 K and 500 K.
The FCC matrix will remain stable from 300 K to 500 K.
Coherent or semi-coherent FCC/BCC boundaries will pin magnetic domain walls.
Coercivity rises dramatically at the FCC/BCC transition in FeCoNi(AlSi)x alloys.
The BCC phase has different exchange interactions and higher magnetocrystalline anisotropy than the soft FCC matrix.
FCC/BCC interfaces will generate exchange bias or domain-wall pinning sufficient to overcome the low coercivity of the FCC matrix.
Compositionally distinct AFM and FM states can arise in compositionally disordered high-entropy oxides.
Percolation of AFM and FM regions in high-entropy oxides creates frustration and exchange bias.
Saturation magnetization will remain comparable to the single-phase FCC baseline or decline only slightly.
The ferromagnetic BCC phase is likely to enhance the alloy's Curie temperature.
The desired behavior requires a coherent BCC phase smaller than 50 nm; coarsening or loss of coherency may cause brittleness or reduce magnetic coupling, coercivity, or saturation magnetization.

contradictions.description: The proposed operating range extends to 500 K, but the predicted Curie-temperature requirement is only greater than 300 K; that requirement does not ensure magnetic order throughout the stated operating range.

The hypothesis and boundary require a coherent BCC phase, while the structural mediator allows semi-coherent boundaries. It is therefore unclear whether semi-coherent interfaces satisfy the design constraint.
The conditions describe 300 K as part of a regime significantly above room temperature, although 300 K is approximately room temperature.
